ministry: Service Alberta and Red Tape Reduction / Technology and Innovation
serviceDescription: The ADSP Project Planner is an AI-agent-powered microservice integrated into the Tenant Management Webapp (TMW) that enables GoA business analysts and developers to discover how ADSP services can address their business problems through natural language conversation. The Planning Agent — powered by Anthropic Claude — conducts guided discovery, builds a structured business model from user input, matches the problem against a configurable library of known GoA business patterns, and generates plain-language ADSP service composition hypotheses. Specialist sub-agents for form-service, pdf-service, comment-service, and notification-service provide implementation-depth guidance. All planning sessions persist across browser sessions, allowing multi-day planning engagements. The service is implemented as a Node.js/TypeScript/Express microservice following all ADSP platform service patterns, including Keycloak JWT authentication, MongoDB persistence, RabbitMQ domain events, and the initializePlatform() SDK initialization.

governingDocuments.name: Freedom of Information and Protection of Privacy Act (FOIP)
governingDocuments.citation: RSA 2000, c F-25 — Governs the collection, use, and disclosure of personal and organizational information held by GoA. Applies to planning session data that may contain GoA program information.

governingDocuments.name: GoA Digital Service Standard
governingDocuments.citation: Government of Alberta Digital Service Standard — Sets requirements for all GoA digital service design, accessibility, and delivery.

governingDocuments.name: GoA Information Management Regulation
governingDocuments.citation: AR 224/2001 — Governs retention and disposition of government records. Planning session data constitutes GoA records subject to defined retention periods.

governingDocuments.name: WCAG 2.1 Level AA
governingDocuments.citation: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines 2.1, Level AA — Mandatory accessibility standard for all GoA public-facing and internal digital interfaces.

governingDocuments.name: OWASP Application Security Verification Standard (ASVS) 4.0
governingDocuments.citation: OWASP ASVS Level 2 — Applicable security baseline for a Protected B GoA information system processing planning session data.

governingDocuments.name: ADSP Platform Service Pattern and Compliance Checklist
governingDocuments.citation: Internal ADSP platform documentation — Mandates initializePlatform() SDK initialization, Keycloak JWT authentication, MongoDB persistence, RabbitMQ domain events, and Configuration Service integration for all ADSP platform services.

digitalPresence.name: Tenant Management Webapp (TMW) — Planner Section
digitalPresence.description: Primary user interface for the ADSP Project Planner, integrated as new navigable pages within the existing TMW application. Accessible to authenticated GoA users with the planner-user, planner-admin, or tenant-admin Keycloak role.

digitalPresence.name: planner-service REST API (v1)
digitalPresence.description: Express 5 REST API providing session management, conversational AI, business model, hypothesis management, pattern management, and session export endpoints. Protected by Keycloak JWT. Base path: /api/v1/.

digitalPresence.name: planner-service Health Check Endpoints
digitalPresence.description: Liveness (/health/live) and readiness (/health/ready) endpoints for ADSP platform monitoring and Kubernetes pod lifecycle management.

supportChannels.name: ADSP Platform Support
supportChannels.description: Primary support channel for ADSP services including planner-service. For questions about service configuration, tenant onboarding, and platform operations.
supportChannels.hours: Monday to Friday, 8:00 AM to 4:30 PM MT (excluding statutory holidays)

supportChannels.name: ADSP Service Catalog Help Desk
supportChannels.description: Online support request submission for GoA staff needing assistance with ADSP services, feature requests, or incident reporting.
supportChannels.hours: Available 24/7 for submission; responses during business hours Monday to Friday

supportChannels.name: Alberta Digital Service Platform — GitHub Issues
supportChannels.description: Technical issue tracking and feature requests for ADSP platform services. Available to GoA developers and platform team members for defect reporting and platform enhancement discussions.
supportChannels.hours: Available 24/7 for submission; responses from ADSP Platform Team during business hours

formsAndDocuments.name: Planning Session Export (JSON)
formsAndDocuments.purpose: Portable JSON document produced by the session export feature (GET /api/v1/sessions/{id}/export). Contains the complete planning session state including business model, solution hypotheses, open questions, and recommended next steps. Used for stakeholder sharing and project documentation.

formsAndDocuments.name: Business Pattern Template (Configuration)
formsAndDocuments.purpose: Structured configuration record stored via the ADSP Configuration Service defining a reusable GoA business process pattern. Includes name, description, domain language, strong signal keywords, ADSP service mappings, and clarifying questions. Managed by Tenant Administrators via the pattern library management interface.

audiences.name: GoA Business Analyst
audiences.description: Government of Alberta business analysts and program managers who use the ADSP Project Planner to describe business problems in natural language, explore AI-generated ADSP service composition recommendations, and guide solution planning for digital service modernization projects. Low to medium technical proficiency with deep GoA domain knowledge.
goals: Describe business problems without requiring prior ADSP technical knowledge
Receive plain-language solution recommendations that can be communicated to program stakeholders
Maintain and resume multi-day planning sessions without re-entering context
Review and correct the AI's business model to ensure accurate problem representation
Export completed session plans for stakeholder sharing
outcomes: Reduced barrier to ADSP adoption through conversational AI discovery
Structured business model capturing the program area's problem accurately
Accepted solution hypothesis ready for developer implementation planning
Portable session export usable in project documentation and stakeholder presentations

audiences.name: GoA Developer
audiences.description: Government of Alberta software developers who use the ADSP Project Planner to explore technical implementation options for new or enhanced GoA applications using ADSP services. High technical proficiency with familiarity in REST APIs, TypeScript, and ADSP service documentation. May provide existing requirements documents or application code as input.
goals: Obtain deep ADSP service integration guidance through specialist agents for form-service, pdf-service, comment-service, and notification-service
Rapidly scope new application features or ADSP integrations against established technical patterns
Navigate seamlessly between the planning session and specialist workspaces with pre-loaded context
Understand solution hypothesis reasoning at implementation-detail level
outcomes: Technical implementation plan grounded in ADSP specialist agent guidance
Identified ADSP service composition pattern suitable for the business problem
Validated integration approach with specialist-endorsed configuration recommendations

audiences.name: ADSP Tenant Administrator
audiences.description: ADSP-registered GoA department administrators responsible for managing the business pattern library and user access for their tenant. Medium technical proficiency with familiarity in TMW administrative interface and ADSP configuration concepts. Infrequent users who act primarily when adding, updating, or maintaining business pattern templates.
goals: Create and maintain tenant-specific business pattern templates to capture departmental process knowledge
Deactivate outdated or incorrect patterns to maintain pattern matching accuracy
Review planning session history across the tenant for oversight and governance purposes
Audit administrative actions through the audit log
outcomes: Business pattern library that accurately reflects the department's recurring business process types
Faster planning sessions for analysts as pattern matching accelerates hypothesis generation
Governance oversight of AI-assisted planning activities within the tenant

audiences.name: ADSP Platform Team
audiences.description: The Government of Alberta technology team responsible for operating, monitoring, and maintaining the Alberta Digital Service Platform. Responsible for enforcing platform standards compliance, ensuring multi-tenant data isolation, and maintaining operational reliability of the planner-service. High technical proficiency with deep ADSP platform architecture knowledge.
goals: Verify planner-service compliance with all ADSP platform service patterns including initializePlatform(), Keycloak JWT, MongoDB, and RabbitMQ
Monitor service health, LLM API performance, and error rates via structured observability
Enforce multi-tenant data isolation and conduct security audit reviews
Configure and enforce role-based access control and session inactivity timeout policies
outcomes: planner-service operates within the ADSP platform operational model without special-casing
All tenant data isolation requirements are provably enforced at API and database layers
Security events and administrative actions are fully auditable with tamper-evident audit logs

audiences.name: GoA Program Manager
audiences.description: Government of Alberta program managers who are indirect beneficiaries of ADSP Project Planner outputs. They receive and review planning session exports prepared by business analysts to make decisions about solution direction and implementation investment. They do not directly interact with the planner-service interface but influence planning through feedback on hypotheses and outputs.
goals: Review solution plan exports to evaluate proposed ADSP service compositions
Approve or redirect solution hypotheses before implementation investment is committed
Understand cost, effort, and implementation order implications of proposed solutions
outcomes: Informed decision-making on ADSP-based digital solution investments
Clear, non-technical documentation of proposed solution direction
Accountability trail showing the reasoning behind technology recommendations

painPoints: GoA program staff cannot easily evaluate whether ADSP services address their business needs without significant prior architectural knowledge, creating a high barrier to adoption
Planning engagements spanning multiple days lose context when browser sessions are closed, requiring analysts to restart discovery from scratch
Developer investigations of ADSP service suitability require manual consultation of multiple service documentation sources with no guided discovery
Tenant administrators have no self-service mechanism to encode department-specific business process patterns into the planning system
keyCapabilities: Conversational AI planning via Anthropic Claude with streaming responses
Incremental business model construction from natural language with user correction capability
GoA business pattern library with automatic matching and hypothesis acceleration
Specialist sub-agents for form-service, pdf-service, comment-service, and notification-service
Persistent planning sessions resumable across browser restarts
ADSP platform-native implementation following all mandatory platform service patterns
additionalContext.technicalStack: Node.js 22 / TypeScript / Express 5 (backend); React 18 / GoA Design System 2.0 @abgov/react-components (UI); MongoDB via Mongoose (persistence); RabbitMQ via ADSP SDK (domain events); Keycloak JWT via passport-jwt (authentication); Anthropic Claude via @anthropic-ai/sdk (LLM inference)
